biography: Carlos Andrade was born in the heart of São Paulo, Brazil, amidst the roar of engines from the nearby Interlagos circuit. His father, a mechanic for a local touring car team, instilled a love for motorsport early on. Carlos began karting at age 10, quickly demonstrating natural talent. He financed his early racing career by working at his father's garage after school. A defining moment came at the Brazilian Karting Championship in 2007, where despite starting last due to a mechanical issue, he clawed his way to victory. This grit and determination propelled him through the ranks, reaching Formula 3 Sudamericana before transitioning to Stock Car Brasil. Now, at 35, Andrade is at the peak of his abilities, leading his own team, Carlos Andrade Racing, and consistently challenging for podiums.
drivingStyle: Andrade possesses a remarkably steady and calculated driving style. He's known for his exceptional tire management, often running longer stints than his competitors. He attacks corners with precision rather than outright aggression, focusing on maintaining momentum and minimizing wheelspin. Under pressure, Andrade remains unflappable, rarely making mistakes, and capitalizing on the errors of others. His ability to read the race and adapt his strategy on the fly makes him a formidable opponent.

careerHighlight: Winning the 2021 Stock Car Brasil championship after a season-long battle, securing his first major title and solidifying his reputation as a top driver.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the 2018 Interlagos race due to a mechanical failure, losing a near-certain victory in front of his home crowd.
